intent: "What does this reply actually mean, in a value I can plan a branch on — and who decided it, from which message, and how sure were they?"
before_repeating: the meaning currently on the thread, with who assigned it and when.

input_schema.title: conversation.classify input
input_schema.description: One thread, and the provider's category it is to be filed under — or none, to take it out of the one it is in. The thread names itself; the campaign is the work item's, carried for context.

external_id.description: The provider's identifier for the thread, as `conversation.list` returned it.

category.description: The provider's category, by the identifier `conversation.list` and `conversation.get` report under `vendor.category.id`, or by its name, compared exactly and without regard to case. Null takes the thread out of its category. Required: which of the three a caller meant is not something to guess.

idempotency_key.description: The work item's own identifier, stable across every attempt.

external_ids.description: Only this plugin's own pins reach it, so another provider's identifier is never visible here.

items.description: One outcome for the one thread.

status.description: `classified`: the thread is filed under `category` now. `cleared`: it is under none. Either holds whatever the thread was under before.

category.description: The category the thread is filed under now, as the provider names it, or null once cleared.

failure_codes.when: The provider holds no thread under this identifier, or not one this account may see. Nothing was filed.
The provider holds no category under the identifier or the name the call carried. Nothing was filed.
More than one of the provider's categories carries the name, so picking one would be guessing and nothing was filed. Name it by its identifier instead.

The category named is one whose filing stops the person at the provider — it opts them out, or ends their participation — and taking the thread out of it again does not undo that. Nothing was filed: stopping a person is `optout.record`'s path.
The provider account's plan or role does not include this capability, so no call by this account can perform it.
The vendor tool refused the call or never started, so nothing the operation asks for was ever attempted. Repeating it runs the same broken call.
The plugin's own credential does not let it file this account's threads.
The provider refused the call for now and it may be attempted again.
The provider could not be reached, or answered with a failure on its own side, before anything was written.
The provider was called and no answer arrived, so the thread may already be filed. Filing it again under the same category leaves it exactly as it is, so the next attempt simply asks again.

The provider refused this call for a reason outside the work item — the account's money or plan, an allowance it counts, a credential it no longer accepts, a channel disconnected or paused — and did nothing for it. The failure's block says what is blocked, why and where a person clears it; a repeat once it clears is a first act. It is said even where the operation also declares an older code for the condition, which then stands for an answer the plugin cannot read as a block.

conformance: The thread is set to exactly the category named, or to none, whatever it was under before: a second performance leaves it as the first did, which is what makes a repeat after a lost answer safe.

A category named by its identifier is one the provider holds, and one named by its name is the one category whose name equals it, compared exactly and without regard to case; nothing is filed otherwise.

Filing a thread asks the provider to change no participation, no enrollment and no read state. A category whose filing would stop the person at the provider — opt them out, end their participation — fails `category_opts_out` before anything is filed: stopping a person is `optout.record`'s path.

A provider may give its reserved categories a meaning of its own — events it sends out, outreach it starts by its own hand — and filing a thread there asks for that meaning too; a campaign that must own every send files under categories of its own.
The category is the provider's own, named in its vocabulary; no neutral meaning is assigned, and nothing is pinned.
